highlights.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
highlights.summary: Growing Harness is a failure‑guided training paradigm that learns reusable executable code for LLM agents, turning recurring control logic into a shared harness while reserving model calls for task‑specific reasoning.
highlights.detail: The method records function‑level execution traces to locate failures, then an optimizer repairs a bounded code window. Successful edits are kept via a held‑out gate that rolls back harmful changes, allowing the harness’s control structure to evolve from task feedback.

highlights.title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
highlights.summary: MAGIC is a dense‑reward reinforcement‑learning framework that constructs mixed‑granularity agent collaboration graphs, selecting fine‑grained or group roles locally to match subtask needs.
highlights.detail: By exploring a combinatorial space of graph constructions with only final‑answer rewards, MAGIC balances detailed control with reusable patterns, enabling dynamic organization of agents without predefined topologies.

highlights.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
highlights.summary: SWE‑Serve is a benchmark comprising 53 repository‑grounded inference engineering tasks across six families, runnable on CPU or a single H100 GPU.
highlights.detail: The tasks reflect recent production changes to SGLang and evaluate agents on full‑stack feature implementation, covering model support, runtime execution, and public API updates, unlike prior benchmarks that focus on isolated kernels or performance tweaks.

highlights.title: ESP32 Replacement for Lighting Display Controller
highlights.summary: Hackaday reports an ESP32‑based replacement for NanoLeaf‑style modular lighting display controllers, enabling addressable LED strip control.
highlights.detail: The design leverages the ESP32’s Wi‑Fi and GPIO capabilities to replicate the snap‑together geometry of NanoLeaf panels while reducing cost and complexity.

highlights.title: Can gzip be a language model?
highlights.summary: A Hacker News discussion asks whether gzip can function as a language model.
highlights.detail: The thread explores the idea of treating a compression algorithm as a predictive model, comparing its statistical properties to those of neural language models.

items.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
items.summary: OpenAI’s blog explains that GPT‑6 improves prompt caching with higher cache‑hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls that cut latency and cost.
items.detail: These enhancements let developers see cache behavior, pause caching at defined points, and adjust settings to optimize performance, especially for high‑throughput applications.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT‑6 Sol and Luna, two models offering different capability‑to‑cost trade‑offs for everyday work.
items.detail: Sol targets higher performance for demanding tasks, while Luna provides a cheaper alternative with modest capability, expanding the range of use‑cases for GPT‑6 technology.

items.title: Parallel cut research time and cost in half with GPT‑6 Astra
items.summary: GPT‑6 Astra let Parallel’s agents complete labor‑market research in half the time and at half the cost compared with earlier models.
items.detail: The improvement stems from Astra’s more efficient reasoning and tool‑use pipelines, demonstrating measurable productivity gains for real‑world data‑synthesis workloads.

items.title: [$] Compiling the kernel with gccrs
items.summary: LWN covers RustConf 2026 talks on gccrs, the Rust frontend for GCC, which aims to compile the Linux kernel but is not yet production‑ready.
items.detail: Presenters highlighted progress on language support and kernel‑specific extensions, noting that further work is needed before gccrs can be used for mainstream kernel builds.

items.title: Security updates for Tuesday
items.summary: Security updates were released for AlmaLinux, Debian, and Fedora on Tuesday, covering dozens of packages across the three distributions.
items.detail: The AlmaLinux update includes libraries such as apr-util and curl, as well as services like sudo and openssh. Debian’s update is limited to the Chromium browser. Fedora’s list spans multimedia, development, and system tools, reflecting a broad maintenance effort.

items.title: Determining the Body Temperature of Tyrannosaurus rex
items.summary: Hackaday explains how paleontologists estimate the body temperature of Tyrannosaurus rex using fossil evidence and physical modeling.
items.detail: The article reviews methods such as isotopic analysis of bone phosphate and comparisons with modern ectotherms and endotherms. It highlights uncertainties due to diagenetic alteration and the limited sample size of well‑preserved specimens.

items.title: Digital Upgrade Brings Medium Format Camera Into the 21st Century
items.summary: A digital upgrade enables the Sitina B220M medium‑format camera to operate with modern 21st‑century workflows.
items.detail: The retrofit adds electronic shutter control and USB‑C connectivity while preserving the camera’s large‑format optics. The modification aims to make the system portable enough for field work without sacrificing image quality.

items.title: Dumpster-dived Window A/C becomes Ground-Source Heat Pump
items.summary: A discarded window‑air‑conditioner was converted into a ground‑source heat pump for residential heating and cooling.
items.detail: The project repurposes the compressor and refrigerant loop to exchange heat with the earth, improving seasonal efficiency. Installation required custom piping and a control algorithm to balance heating and cooling demands.

items.title: Hydrozoan: Latency-Adaptive DAG Consensus under Mixed Byzantine and Crash Faults
items.summary: Hydrozoan introduces a DAG consensus protocol with dual commit paths, achieving two‑message delay when ≤p validators are faulty and three‑message delay otherwise, on n = 3f + c + 2p + 1 validators.
items.detail: The protocol works under a hybrid fault model of f Byzantine and c crash‑faulty validators, allowing multiple leaders per round. A novel graded indirect rule reconciles the two paths on the same DAG, ensuring consistent decisions without view changes. Experiments show geographic placement influences which path is faster.

items.title: I asked Meta’s Muse for its filesystem and it sent me 6.8GB
items.summary: Meta’s Muse AI responded to a filesystem request by sending a 6.8 GB archive of its internal file structure.
items.detail: The interaction was posted on Hacker News, illustrating how large language models can expose extensive internal data when prompted. The size of the response raises questions about data leakage and model safety. No further context was provided in the original post.

items.title: Don't let your Memory defy you: Fragmentation-Aware Serverless Allocation with Elastic Memory Locality
items.summary: Memoryless is a fragmentation‑aware serverless manager that exposes memory locality as a control‑plane primitive to better utilize disaggregated memory.
items.detail: By offering function variants with different compute‑memory ratios, Memoryless matches workloads to residual capacity on nodes, reducing external fragmentation. The system builds on Knative and demonstrates SLO‑preserving scheduling despite mixed local and remote memory usage. Evaluation shows improved node utilization compared to traditional memory‑centric allocations.

items.title: Flux: Optimal Scheduling of Optical Circuit Switches for LLM Training
items.summary: Flux scheduler reduces LLM training iteration time by up to 10× by aligning optical circuit‑switch reconfigurations with compute phases.
items.detail: Flux reuses existing circuits and amortizes reconfiguration latency behind overlapping compute and communication, making it effective across a range of switch speeds. The approach contrasts with prior OCS schedulers that ignore the compute timeline, leading to under‑utilized bandwidth and larger buffers. Simulations on typical LLM workloads confirm the performance gains.

items.title: Databases with Missing Values that are Governed by Missingness Mechanisms
items.summary: The paper proposes a probabilistic database model that incorporates missingness mechanisms via a Bayesian network, enabling tractable query answering on certain optimal world classes.
items.detail: Missing values are governed by a Missingness Graph, distinguishing this approach from traditional NULL handling. The authors identify two optimal classes of possible worlds that capture both statistical plausibility and probabilistic uncertainty. They provide tractability results for some queries and complexity bounds for others, outlining when efficient evaluation is feasible.

items.title: Proof-of-Retention: A Framework for Auditable Cross-Organization Data Sharing
items.summary: Proof‑of‑Retention is a framework that provides auditable, cross‑organization data‑sharing by preserving and verifying provenance metadata.
items.detail: The protocol enables parties to prove that shared data remains unchanged and compliant with regulations such as GDPR and the US Data Privacy Act. It includes interactive challenges that detect unilateral modifications, ensuring that provenance records stay current. The design targets AI training pipelines that require high‑quality, legally compliant datasets.

items.detail: The repository provides the foundational components for building modular, agent‑based applications. It includes a lightweight runtime and APIs for integrating custom agents.
